abi: Far runtime register helper. Shifts DX:AX left by CL, clears CH, consumes CX for a nonzero count, and returns DX:AX via RETF without popping arguments.
boundary_evidence: The complete 135-byte lshl.asm member in the 6.00A PDS DOS LIBH.LIB has 11 initialized _TEXT bytes, empty _DATA, sole ungrouped __aFlshl at offset zero, and zero fixups. Whole member is byte-identical in 6.00 DOS LIBH.LIB and the 6.00A July DDK MLIBCER.LIB.

The full original CODE extent is root image [0x21b40,0x21b4b). The prior multiply exits with RETF 8 at 0x21b3d. JCXZ at 0x21b42 and LOOP at 0x21b48 stay inside the shift helper and both paths reach RETF at 0x21b4a. Root 0x21b4b is a separate zero alignment byte before the BP frame at 0x21b4c.

Game-side CALL FARs at root image 0x11e46 and 0x121e3 encode the wrapper 1fe6:1cec (MZ relocation indices 1439 and 1440). The wrapper loads DX:AX through a near pointer and CX from BP+8, then uses PUSH CS; CALL near at root 0x21b5b. Next IP 0x1cff plus signed displacement -31 is 0x1ce0 in the independently anchored 1fe6 frame. The wrapper stores DX:AX back and exits with RETF 4.

There are zero original relocations touching the full extent and no physical overlaps with manifest owners. The caller frame is independently anchored, while original library order and behavior remain unproved.
